html:
SMTO-BOOT-0025 — The installer can't see any NVIDIA graphics cards

GUID: d1071c53-b446-48ee-9cc4-218e05eb8b09
Slug: boot-cuda-devices-missing
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The installer found no NVIDIA graphics card it can use, so it stopped. If this happened during the final check, vLLM is already installed and only the card access needs fixing.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Run env | grep CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES. If it shows a value, make sure it lists only card numbers that nvidia-smi shows, or remove it with unset CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES. This setting decides which cards programs may use; an empty or wrong value hides every card.
  2. Run nvidia-smi and check that your card is listed. If you use a container or WSL, make sure graphics card access is turned on for it. If the computer's own driver tool can't list the card, the installer can't use it either.
  3. If the error appeared after "Checking dependencies, vLLM imports, and CUDA access", vLLM is installed. Once the card is visible, run ./src/vllm/install-vllm.sh --verify-only with your environment name. Check-only mode retests the existing install without downloading anything; a fresh install would refuse the existing name.
  4. If it appeared earlier, run conda env list before installing again. If your environment name is listed, use a new name or remove that half-built environment first. The installer won't install into a name that already exists, even a half-built one.

What success looks like

  • The installer prints a "GPU 0:" line for your card and continues, or check-only mode ends with "vLLM verification complete".

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the SMTO-BOOT-0025 line, plus the output of nvidia-smi, and send it to the person who manages this computer. Don't switch to different graphics cards than the ones you meant to use just to get past this check.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • No CUDA devices were visible to the vLLM installer: the driver probe returned CUDA_ERROR_NO_DEVICE (100) or an empty GPU list, or final verification found torch.cuda.is_available() false in the installed environment.

What this means

  • CUDA probing reports no-device status, returns an empty GPU inventory, or installed PyTorch reports CUDA unavailable. Hardware planning or installed-environment verification stops. If the failure is in final verification, the environment and installed packages remain. No visible CUDA devices does not establish whether GPUs are physically absent, hidden, inaccessible or unsupported by the installed runtime.

Why this can happen

  • CUDA probing reports no-device status, returns an empty GPU inventory, or installed PyTorch reports CUDA unavailable.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, device access and driver/PyTorch visibility; physical GPUs may still exist outside this scope.

How to fix it

  • Check CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (an empty or invalid value hides every GPU), nvidia-smi, and host or container GPU passthrough. If the failure was in final verification, the environment and its packages remain: fix device visibility and rerun install-vllm.sh --verify-only with that name instead of reinstalling; otherwise remove any partially created environment or use a new name.
  • Check the intended CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES selection and host/container GPU access.

Retry and execution caution

  • Restore intended CUDA device visibility; use --verify-only to recheck an environment that already exists.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended CUDA devices are visible through the supported installation environment.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Hardware planning or installed-environment verification stops. If the failure is in final verification, the environment and installed packages remain.
  • No visible CUDA devices does not establish whether GPUs are physically absent, hidden, inaccessible or unsupported by the installed runtime.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
